power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: The sample size was calculated for multiple regression with six predictors, assuming α=0.05, Cohen's f² =0.15, and 95% power, yielding a minimum sample of 150 participants. Although the recruitment target was 188 after allowing for 20% non-response, 164 participants were enrolled, exceeding the minimum required sample. Site-specific recruitment targets were allocated according to the relative clinic caseloads: (Kenyatta National Hospital, n=40; Westland's Level 4 Hospital, n=23; Machakos level 5 hospital, n=68; Kajiado level 5 hospital, n=33). Eligible participants registered at each clinic were identified through a multimodal recruitment strategy using routine clinic attendance, telephone invitations from hospital records, announcements on diabetes support platforms, and peer referral. Recruitment was conducted by trained research assistants, from September to December 2025, using a consecutive sampling approach, enrolling all eligible participants present during the study recruitment period or identified in records. This approach continued until the target sample for each site was achieved.

live_data_statements: Participants were eligible if they were aged 18-34 years, had a clinician-documented diagnosis of T1D in the medical record, were receiving ongoing insulin therapy, and had a clinical presentation consistent with insulin deficiency [15], including acute onset of diabetes and/or classical hyperglycaemic symptoms at diagnosis.
Although the recruitment target was 188 after allowing for 20% non-response, 164 participants were enrolled, exceeding the minimum required sample.

Variations in responses and qualitative feedback from participants were reviewed to identify unclear, ambiguous, or contextually inappropriate items and were used to refine the wording, clarity, and overall usability of the questionnaire before data collection.
Participants had a mean HbA1c of 11.50 ± 3.44% with 134 (81.7%) having HbA1c ≥9.0%, while only 8 (4.9%) achieved HbA1c <7.0%.

Early cardio-renal complication markers were also frequent: 46 (28.0%) participants had a single elevated UACR, while 92 (56.1%) participants had LDL-C above 2.6 mmol/L and 105 (64.0%) participants had an LDL/HDL ratio ≥2.
The greatest SDOH burden was seen in economic stability, where 76.8% of participants had moderate-to-high burden followed by social and community context at 52.4%.
Approximately 28% of participants had elevated UACR, suggesting a substantial burden of possible early diabetic kidney involvement.
Written informed consent was obtained from all participants before enrolment in the study.
In contrast, most participants had low burden in education and health literacy [128 (78.1%)], neighbourhood and physical environment [119 (72.6%)], and healthcare system [119 (72.6%)] domains.
